transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Aurora Head of ML), Priya Shah (Aurora Platform), Oliver Grant (Aurora CTO), Sofia Martinez (Procurement)
Recording: (auto) link omitted

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, and usage analytics. Customer wants to understand how Redwood reports per-route cost and how to map to their internal chargeback. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, VPC options, and benchmarking next steps. Agreed to share pricing + benchmark runbook and to scope a short PoC.

Topics covered:
- Per-route dashboards and tags
- Token-level cost breakdown and chargeback mapping
- Route-level latency / error metrics and SLO alerting
- Dedicated capacity sizing vs hosted burst options
- Security: audit logs, SSO, KMS
- Next steps and benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can kick off  yes thanks for making time. I'm Maya, I'll run you through the console and Arjun will jump in on the latency / benchmarking bits.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Thanks Maya, excited. Quick call purpose, we want visibility on per-route cost so we can charge back to product teams. Also latency targets for our chat feature.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll share my screen and start in the Console > Usage analytics. Bear with me if the auto-transcription lags.
[00:24] (screen share sound)
[00:30] Arjun Patel: Hi all, quick intro for me  I work on infra/serving optimizations. I'll go deeper on batching, kv cache behavior and Dedicated sizing.
[00:38] Priya Shah: Quick FYI from infra side we run mostly 8k context, average request length 280 tokens but tails to 2k for a small percent. We need p95 under 350ms for the chat route.
[00:51] Jordan Lee: Noted, thanks Priya, that's helpful.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Ok, pulling up per-route dashboard. On the left you can filter by model, route name, team tag, and timeframe. You'll see a breakdown: total tokens, request count, avg tokens per request, latency p50/p95/p99, and a cost estimate column.
[01:15] Liam O'Connor: Is that cost estimate based on Redwood's unit pricing or our committed Dedicated rates?
[01:21] Maya Chen: By default it shows hosted list pricing, but you can switch the pricing profile to your committed Dedicated SKUs or a custom rate. So for chargeback you can map to your internal cost centers.
[01:32] Priya Shah: How do we tag routes? Can tags be applied at the API key level or via the SDK?
[01:37] Arjun Patel: Both; tag at route config or add tags into the request metadata header. We ingest tags and they appear in the per-route rollup. Sometimes the SDK auto-sets route name, which we can override.
[01:49] Oliver Grant: About the token cost calc, do you include prefix caching savings? Like if a lot of our requests share a prompt prefix, how is that accounted?
[01:58] Jordan Lee: Good question  the console shows an estimated raw token count plus an "effective token" column that factors in prefix/KV cache hits using the request dedupe heuristics. It's an estimate  we also export raw request logs if you want exact accounting.
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: We'd prefer to do chargeback on effective cost rather than raw tokens. Does Redwood expose the dedupe ratio per route?
[02:20] Maya Chen: Yep, there's a cache hit metric and a derived savings % per route. You can export a CSV of those metrics daily.
[02:28] Priya Shah: Can you show the cost breakdown by model version? We sometimes shift versions during rollouts.
[02:35] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Model version is an axis in the dashboard  you can split by model and version, and we show delta in cost and latency. So when you do canaries, you can see the cost delta in real time.
[02:47] Oliver Grant: Ok that's helpful. On Dedicated vs Hosted: what's the basic tradeoff for us? We care about predictable performance and data control.
[02:57] Arjun Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput/latency  you can pin model variants and we reserve capacity. Hosted is more elastic and cheaper for spiky workloads but less predictable for hard SLOs. Also Dedicated keeps data isolated and works well with VPC peering.
[03:14] Priya Shah: For the Dedicated, do you support our KMS/HSM? We need envelope encryption with our key control.
[03:20] Maya Chen: Yes, Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS integration and audit logs. We'll share the security docs.
[03:27] Sofia Martinez: From procurement side, do you provide sample SOW language for Dedicated engagements and table of SKUs?
[03:33] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll attach pricing + sample SOW in the follow-up.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: Back to console, can you show the per-route alerting  we need to be notified when cost rate crosses threshold or p95 latency breaches SLOs.
[03:44] Jordan Lee: Under Alerts you can create a policy: choose the metric (cost rate per minute, p95 latency), specify an aggregation window and threshold, and set notification channels (Slack, PagerDuty, webhook). Policies can be scoped to route tags or model.
[03:56] Priya Shah: Can alerts be tied to budget  like daily spend cap per route?
[03:59] Jordan Lee: You can set budget alerts and automatic throttling/fallback  e.g., when route spend hits 85% of daily budget, send alert; at 100% you can auto-fallback to smaller model variant or block requests.
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: How do you handle model fallbacks without degrading quality too much? We want guardrails.
[04:18] Arjun Patel: You configure fallback chains  primary model, then quantized variant, then a cheaper model. You can attach eval suites to monitor quality shift and set a hard stop if quality regresses beyond tolerance.
[04:29] Oliver Grant: Speaking of evals, can we tie console alerts to prompt-based regressions?
[04:34] Maya Chen: Yes  Redwood Optimize supports regression alerts tied to prompt sets / evals. When a route's output quality drops below threshold on your test prompts, it triggers alerts. We'll share an example eval config.
[04:45] Priya Shah: On the cost calc, are GPUs amortized into token unit pricing or is it a separate cost center in the dashboard?
[04:52] Jordan Lee: The default cost model shows per-token unit cost derived from your plan. For Dedicated, we also provide an amortized cost view where infra fixed monthly is spread across units; we show both so you can decide how to charge internal teams.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: Good. Can you export per-request logs? We want to run our own offline attribution.
[05:11] Arjun Patel: Yes, we have exports: per-request events with route, model, tokens, cache hits, latency, and trace IDs. For Private/Dedicated we can set up s3 exports into your VPC.
[05:22] Priya Shah: Important: our compliance team wants audit trail for admin actions. How long are audit logs retained?
[05:28] Maya Chen: Audit logs retention depends on plan; enterprise can configure retention windows and long-term storage. We'll include retention options in the security pack.
[05:35] Liam O'Connor: Competitors question  we looked at Anthropic and OpenAI; any differences in your per-route visibility vs their consoles?
[05:43] Maya Chen: We try to be more production-first: per-route cost attribution, prefix caching visibility, and tight hooks for rollout/rollbacks with eval-based quality checks. Others have good UX but less focus on chargeback and cache-aware cost.
[05:55] Oliver Grant: Any gotchas on attribution when we do multi-model ensembles? For example, we shard on intent and call two models in series.
[06:03] Arjun Patel: The console supports composite route definitions. We tag each sub-call and the per-route view can either attribute cost to the parent or show the breakdown of the ensemble. It's configurable.
[06:15] Priya Shah: Let's talk sizing: we have sustained 600 RPS across chat endpoints with avg 280 tokens, peaks to 2.5k RPS during promos. Any initial Dedicated recommendation?
[06:27] Arjun Patel: We'll need to run a quick benchmark with representative traces. Rough ballpark  depends on model size and batching profile. For inference-opt GPT-style 13B equivalents, you'd likely need several GPUs; I'll propose an initial Dedicated SKU in the follow-up after we see the traces.
[06:42] Liam O'Connor: Can you walk through the benchmarking steps? We need to know what's required for us to provide.
[06:47] Arjun Patel: Sure. We ask for 1) representative request trace (anonymized) with timestamps and tokens, 2) target SLOs, 3) expected concurrency, 4) models you want to test. We run end-to-end benchmark and give latency/cost curves and recommended batch sizes and KV cache configs.
[07:02] Priya Shah: I'll need to check what we can share. If we can't share traces, can we run a synthetic workload on your side?
[07:07] Maya Chen: Yes, synthetic is possible but less accurate. We prefer traces. We can also offer an on-prem agent to run benchmarks inside your VPC if data sensitivity is a concern.
[07:18] Oliver Grant: For the PoC, timeline wise we want something in May. Is that realistic?
[07:22] Maya Chen: Yes, if you can share traces end of week, we can run initial benchmarks and propose Dedicated sizing by early May. That aligns with our standard PoC scoping.
[07:31] Sofia Martinez: Procurement note  we need a draft SOW before legal kickoff.
[07:34] Maya Chen: We'll include sample SOW in the follow-up.
[07:36] (short pause)
[07:40] Jordan Lee: Back to console, I want to show a sample CSV export. (narration) Here you see columns: timestamp, route, model, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit_bool, effective_tokens, cost_estimate_usd, latency_ms, trace_id.
[07:59] Priya Shah: Great, can the effective_tokens column be computed with our custom cache TTLs?
[08:04] Jordan Lee: We can configure the dedupe heuristics and TTL settings so the effective calc uses your TTLs. It becomes part of the export.
[08:12] Liam O'Connor: On security we asked about SSO and RBAC  can you show admin roles?
[08:18] Maya Chen: Under Teams -> RBAC, you can define roles (viewer, operator, admin) and map to SAML groups. Admin actions are logged in audit logs with user and IP.
[08:28] Priya Shah: Does the console support service account keys with limited scope?
[08:31] Jordan Lee: Yes, service keys can be scoped to specific routes and have expiration.
[08:35] Liam O'Connor: A question on cost reporting frequency  is it near real-time or daily?
[08:40] Jordan Lee: Cost metrics are near real-time (a few minutes lag) for hosted; for Dedicated amortized metrics we update hourly.
[08:48] Priya Shah: Any differences for on-prem/private? We might run a hybrid.
[08:53] Arjun Patel: For Private/on-prem, you run the inference nodes; the control plane still aggregates metrics if you enable telemetry. If telemetry is off, we provide local export tools.
[09:06] Oliver Grant: Ok good. A few nitty-gritty items: can we whitelist IP ranges for API traffic?
[09:12] Maya Chen: Yes, VPC and IP allow lists supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted has IP allow list for account-level.
[09:20] Liam O'Connor: Any SLO guarantees for p99?
[09:24] Maya Chen: Our Dedicated SLAs cover uptime and latency targets per contract  specific p99 targets we can include in SOW for priority tiers.
[09:32] Priya Shah: For the follow-up, we'll share token histogram and desired p95 and p99 numbers.
[09:37] Maya Chen: Great. I'll include an action list after the call.
[09:41] (minutes later, wrap up)
[09:45] Maya Chen: Quick recap: Maya to send pricing + SOW and security docs; Arjun to share benchmark runbook; Priya to share token histogram/representative traces; schedule PoC scoping week of 2026-05-11.
[09:56] Liam O'Connor: That works. Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Maya Chen: Thanks  we'll follow up via email.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cache), names slightly off in auto notes, filler words present.
